longForm.overview:
🇪🇬 is the emoji of red-white-black coded national-identity read — the red-white-and-black banner, the eagle-of-Saladin coded flex, and the universal 'red-white-black pulse' tag for Egypt pride. Where 🇺🇳 reads as neutral-coded diplomacy read and 🏳️‍🌈 reads as rainbow-coded pride read, 🇪🇬 captures the moment when the sender wants to communicate red-white-black coded identity — a 'red-white-black 🇪🇬' heritage check-in or a 'eagle-of-Saladin pulse 🇪🇬' Pharaohs reveal. The red-white-and-black banner cue borrows from Egypt's national flag tradition and the modern heritage-coded aesthetic, which is exactly why the emoji reads as red-white-black coded rather than literal travel-coded flag.

In real-world usage 🇪🇬 lives in the spaces where the sender wants to communicate red-white-black energy. A partner sends it on a 'red-white-black 🇪🇬' heritage check-in. A friend sends it on a 'eagle-of-Saladin pulse 🇪🇬' pride reveal. A coworker sends it on a 'red-white-black coded 🇪🇬' heritage-month thread. The red-white-and-black banner cue is what makes the emoji feel red-white-black coded — it is not just 'flag,' it is 'red-white-black coded Egypt-pride moment.'

What separates 🇪🇬 from the rest of the flag family is the red-white-black register. The emoji is not saying 'rainbow pride' (🏳️‍🌈), 'black rebellion' (🏴), or 'checkered finish' (🏁). It is saying 'red-white-black coded Egypt-coded identity,' which carries a specific national-flag tradition. That is why 🇪🇬 travels especially well on partner heritage check-ins, Pharaohs reveals, and any context where the sender wants the message to land with red-white-black energy.

longForm.whenNotToUse:
Skip 🇪🇬 in sympathy, condolence, or break-up contexts. The red-white-black coded banner cue is the wrong tone for any conversation where the moment is somber. A quiet ❤️ or a sentence that acknowledges the moment is a better fit.

Avoid 🇪🇬 in 'racing' or finish-coded contexts where the red-white-black energy feels off. A 'red-white-black 🇪🇬' message works for heritage reveal; for finish-coded contexts use 🏁 or a sentence.

Skip 🇪🇬 when you want to communicate a different country. The red-white-black coded register is too Egypt-coded for moments that need a literal national flag; use 🇺🇳 or another country flag when the nation needs to land clean.
